newsitem.title: USA: U.N. agency said making appeal for N.Korea food.
newsitem.headline: U.N. agency said making appeal for N.Korea food.

text.p: The World Food Programme has formally appealed for $41.6 million in new food aid for North Korea and the United States was certain to make a contribution, U.S. officials said on Tuesday.

"I understand the World Food Programme today issued a new emergency appeal for humanitarian assistance to North Korea. The World Food Programme is seeking donations of 100,00 metric tons of food valued at roughly $41.6 million," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters.

Burns, noting that the United States has responded positively to all other previous food appeals for North Korea, said the administration was "seriously" studying the request and would make a decision very soon. A senior official, speaking anonymously, added: "I believe the United States will make a decision to contribute."
Burns said Washington believed there was a food crisis in North Korea. He said the new appeal was designed to feed 1.7 million North Korea civilians, including 630,000 children under the age of five.

He acknowledged that the World Food Programme, a United Nations agency, had limited its appeal to only a fraction of North Korea's needs, estimated at 2.3 million tons. This was because "they want to focus on meeting the immediate needs of targeted groups and they have targeted young children," he said.
